questions.stimulus:
Text 1
In a study of open-plan municipal libraries, architect Leo Sterling argues that removing interior walls fosters collaborative civic engagement. According to architect Leo Sterling, expanding this practice across comparable sites would yield immediate, measurable gains. Text 2
Evaluating the same open-plan municipal libraries, acoustics researcher Priya Nair observes that unpartitioned reading halls raise ambient noise enough to reduce comprehension on complex tasks. Consequently, acoustics researcher Priya Nair cautions against adopting the practice without targeted safeguards.
questions.prompt: Based on the texts, on what point do architect Leo Sterling and acoustics researcher Priya Nair most clearly differ regarding open-plan municipal libraries?

choices.text: Both authors conclude that open-plan municipal libraries is obsolete compared with nineteenth-century methods.
architect Leo Sterling emphasizes the primary performance advantage of open-plan municipal libraries, whereas acoustics researcher Priya Nair focuses on a secondary operational trade-off.
architect Leo Sterling studies only laboratory models, whereas acoustics researcher Priya Nair refuses to consider empirical data.
architect Leo Sterling opposes open-plan municipal libraries on financial grounds, whereas acoustics researcher Priya Nair supports it unconditionally.

questions.stimulus:
Text 1
In a study of digital restoration of silent films, film archivist Mateo Silva argues that frame-interpolation algorithms make damaged reels accessible to modern audiences. According to film archivist Mateo Silva, expanding this practice across comparable sites would yield immediate, measurable gains. Text 2
Evaluating the same digital restoration of silent films, cinema historian Hannah Berg observes that smoothing original frame rates erases the deliberate rhythmic cranking choices of early camera operators. Consequently, cinema historian Hannah Berg cautions against adopting the practice without targeted safeguards.
questions.prompt: If cinema historian Hannah Berg's findings are accurate, what implication follows for the implementation of digital restoration of silent films advocated by film archivist Mateo Silva?

choices.text: The benefits described by film archivist Mateo Silva are mathematically impossible to measure.
Achieving the benefits film archivist Mateo Silva describes without incurring the costs cinema historian Hannah Berg identifies requires modifying how digital restoration of silent films is executed.
cinema historian Hannah Berg's concern applies only to systems that have already been decommissioned.
digital restoration of silent films can be deployed at maximum scale without any monitoring or mitigation.

questions.stimulus:
While researching bioluminescent dinoflagellate defense mechanisms (study note set 3), a student has taken the following notes:
• Lingulodinium polyedra is a marine dinoflagellate species that emits brief blue light flashes when mechanically agitated.
• Laboratory shear-flow experiments show that a single cell flash lasts approximately 100 milliseconds at 475 nanometers wavelength.
• When grazing copepods disturb the water, the resulting flashes startle the copepods and reduce their feeding rates by 55%.
• The flashes also illuminate the copepods, making them visible to nocturnal predatory fish from up to two meters away.
• Cultures kept under constant light lose their circadian bioluminescence rhythm within four days.
questions.prompt: The student wants to explain how bioluminescence protects Lingulodinium polyedra in two distinct ways. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.text: Nocturnal predatory fish can spot illuminated prey from distances of up to two meters in dark water.
Laboratory cultures of Lingulodinium polyedra lose their circadian rhythm if kept under constant illumination for four days.
When disturbed by grazing copepods, Lingulodinium polyedra emits blue flashes that both directly startle the copepods—cutting feeding by 55%—and expose the grazers to nocturnal predatory fish.
Lingulodinium polyedra emits 100-millisecond flashes at a wavelength of 475 nanometers when mechanically agitated.

questions.stimulus: In medieval European scriptoria, parchment made from calfskin (vellum) was prized for illuminated manuscripts because its smooth, low-lipid surface accepted gold leaf and mineral pigments evenly. However, archival multispectral imaging of twelfth-century parish registries—documents intended for routine administrative tracking rather than liturgical display—shows that scribes overwhelmingly selected coarser sheepskin parchment, which split easily if scraped to remove ink.
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Because parish registries did not require decorative illumination, scribes prioritized sheepskin's resistance to undetected erasure and lower cost over vellum's smooth finish.
Multispectral imaging cannot distinguish between calfskin and sheepskin in illuminated liturgical manuscripts.
Twelfth-century scribes lacked access to mineral pigments when compiling administrative parish registries.
Vellum manuscripts deteriorated more rapidly in parish archives than sheepskin registries did.

questions.stimulus: Agronomists tested four cover-crop mixtures across 120 days to evaluate soil nitrogen retention and late-season weed suppression in upper Midwest plots. The researchers concluded that pairing a legume with a cereal grass allows farmers to capture nearly the full weed-suppression benefit of the grass without sacrificing the high nitrogen retention of the legume.
questions.prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the researchers' conclusion?

choices.text: The Clover + Winter Rye mix achieved 86% weed suppression (close to Winter Rye's 89%) while retaining 64 kg/ha of nitrogen (close to Crimson Clover's 68 kg/ha).
Tillage Radish retained 51 kg/ha of nitrogen and suppressed 72% of weeds, outperforming Winter Rye in nitrogen retention.
Crimson Clover retained 68 kg/ha of nitrogen, the highest amount of any treatment in the 120-day trial.
Winter Rye alone suppressed 89% of weeds, whereas Crimson Clover alone suppressed only 54% of weeds.

questions.stimulus: In a recent study, ornithologist Farah Al-Mansoor argues that urban blackbirds shift their dawn chorus to higher acoustic frequencies to avoid masking by low-frequency traffic rumble (dataset series 3).
questions.prompt: Which finding from the research team's records, if true, would most directly support ornithologist Farah Al-Mansoor's claim?

choices.text: Recordings from 40 city parks show an average minimum song frequency of 2.4 kHz, compared with 1.8 kHz in quiet rural forests 30 kilometers away.
Blackbirds in both city parks and rural forests begin singing approximately thirty minutes before civil sunrise.
Plumage reflectance measurements did not differ significantly between urban and rural adult males.
Clutch sizes in suburban gardens averaged 4.1 eggs per nest across the three-year observation window.
